As I was working with Koszul complex, I would like to deal with its invarience under base change. Since discussed earlier here, it was intended have object rfl with tensor product, but in application, a very direct inference took more than 200000 heartbeat, with its application consuming almost 600000.
So I am indeed needing a extend scalars functor for algebra, thus won't have that much instance issue. My question is are we really needing this general version for extending scalars by ring hom? Would we care about this sort of "duplication" if I add the version for algebra?
For the design itself I have more question, is this tensoring with Modulecat.restrictScalars f (Modulecat.of S S) for f : R => S really the correct way? Since it already involve Module.comHom. Would f.toAlgebra be better?
Do anyone have comment about this? Thanks
My experience is that these are complex questions and you might get more attention if you write a mwe showing the phenomenon you're talking about

Thanks for the suggestion.
However I found this is caused by some problems mixed together, so I may need to decompose first. Also currently I think the main problem isn't from ModuleCat.extendScalars.

The current problem might not be that related now. It still happens after getting rid of category theory. If I remove the typr hint it would cosume almost 300k heartbeat, even now it si consuming over 100k.

module

public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.Alternating.Uncurry.Fin
public import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.ExteriorPower.Basis

universe u v

open Module ExteriorAlgebra

variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] {M : Type v} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (φ : M →ₗ[R] R)

/-- The alternating map on `(n + 1)`-tuples whose induced linear map is the Koszul differential. -/
noncomputable def koszulComplexAuxAlternating (n : ℕ) : M [⋀^Fin (n + 1)]→ₗ[R] ⋀[R]^n M :=
  AlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin (φ.smulRight (exteriorPower.ιMulti R n))

/-- The auxiliary differential used to build the Koszul complex. -/
noncomputable def koszulComplexAux (n : ℕ) : ⋀[R]^(n + 1) M →ₗ[R] ⋀[R]^n M :=
  exteriorPower.alternatingMapLinearEquiv (koszulComplexAuxAlternating φ n)

section DifferentialGradedAlgebra

end DifferentialGradedAlgebra

namespace koszulComplex

variable (S : Type (max u v)) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S] {l : List R} {l' : List S}

open TensorProduct

variable {S}

noncomputable def Set.powersetCardEquiv (eqmap : l.map (algebraMap R S) = l') (i : ℕ) :
    Set.powersetCard (Fin l'.length) i ≃ Set.powersetCard (Fin l.length) i where
  toFun := Set.powersetCard.map i (finCongr (by simp [← eqmap])).toEmbedding
  invFun := Set.powersetCard.map i (finCongr (by simp [← eqmap])).toEmbedding
  left_inv x := by
    ext
    simp
  right_inv x := by
    ext
    simp

noncomputable def exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso (eqmap : l.map (algebraMap R S) = l') (i : ℕ) :
    ⋀[S]^i (Fin l'.length → S) ≃ₗ[S] S ⊗[R] ⋀[R]^i (Fin l.length → R) :=
  Module.Basis.equiv ((Pi.basisFun S (Fin l'.length)).exteriorPower i)
    (((Pi.basisFun R (Fin l.length)).exteriorPower i).baseChange S)
    (Set.powersetCardEquiv eqmap i)

--set_option maxHeartbeats 300000 in
lemma exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso_comm (eqmap : l.map (algebraMap R S) = l') (i : ℕ) :
    (((exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso eqmap i).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
      koszulComplexAux (Fintype.linearCombination S l'.get) i :
        ⋀[S]^(i + 1) (Fin l'.length → S) →ₗ[S]
          S ⊗[R] ⋀[R]^i (Fin l.length → R)) =
        ((koszulComplexAux (Fintype.linearCombination R l.get) i).baseChange S ∘ₗ
          (exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso eqmap (i + 1)).toLinearMap :
            ⋀[S]^(i + 1) (Fin l'.length → S) →ₗ[S]
              S ⊗[R] ⋀[R]^i (Fin l.length → R))) := by
  sorry

end koszulComplex

OK so I think your problem is universes. Look at this definition in your code, but with universes switched on:

koszulComplex.exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso.{u, v} {R : Type u} [CommRing.{u} R] {S : Type (max u v)}
  [CommRing.{max u v} S] [Algebra.{u, max u v} R S] {l : List.{u} R} {l' : List.{max u v} S}
  (eqmap : Eq.{max (u + 1) (v + 1)} (List.map.{u, max u v} (⇑(algebraMap.{u, max u v} R S)) l) l') (i : ℕ) :
  LinearEquiv.{max u v, max u v, max u v, max u v} (RingHom.id.{max u v} S)
    (↥(exteriorPower.{max u v, max u v} S i (Fin (List.length.{max u v} l') → S)))
    (TensorProduct.{u, max u v, u} R S ↥(exteriorPower.{u, u} R i (Fin (List.length.{u} l) → R)))

Even given all the inputs to that explicitly, Lean is unable to solve for v because nothing appears with type v, everything is type max u v or whatever. So what I think is happening is that there are terms which are syntactically identical except one has a v in and the other has a ?u.69 in and Lean refuses to solve for v because max u v = max u ? has more than one solution in general (eg ? could be v or max u v). So it just unfolds absolutely everything until it has run out of ideas (which is incredibly expensive in your situation) and then decides to go for v anyway.

So in the long term you might need a redesign so that Lean can figure out v in your definitions, but in the short term just adding explicit v's like this (in two places):

lemma exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso_comm (eqmap : l.map (algebraMap R S) = l') (i : ℕ) :
    (((exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso.{_,v} eqmap i).toLinearMap ∘ₗ
      koszulComplexAux (Fintype.linearCombination S l'.get) i :
        ⋀[S]^(i + 1) (Fin l'.length → S) →ₗ[S]
          S ⊗[R] ⋀[R]^i (Fin l.length → R)) =
        ((koszulComplexAux (Fintype.linearCombination R l.get) i).baseChange S ∘ₗ
          (exteriorPowerBaseChange_iso.{_,v} eqmap (i + 1)).toLinearMap :
            ⋀[S]^(i + 1) (Fin l'.length → S) →ₗ[S]
              S ⊗[R] ⋀[R]^i (Fin l.length → R))) := by

My instinct would be to simply demand that S is in the same universe as R. This is a very simple fix. I cannot imagine a situation mathematically where this would be false, but you'll always get the maximally polymorphic people arguing that we should instead be jumping through hoops.
I agree with Kevin here, anything that is not an indexing type and causes even mild complications should just be universe monomorphised.

Oh good to hear! Of course I was just being intentionally provocative in my last post; what is really going on is that sometimes I fight hard for polymorphism and sometimes I am too lazy, and my opinions on it change day by day. It's good to have someone with coherent and perhaps more consistent ideas than mine chiming in :-)

A good news (sort of) is that I actually resolved this using a better way (more general isomorphism directly at exterior power level, also passing an intermediate step via tensor product). But you are correct that this doesn't matters much in my later applications. (I previously thought there are some universe issue due to Cohen structure theorem, but actually no :)
The question left is probably what is the convention here? How it is related to indexing type?

For indexing types I, there tend to be two relevant cases I : Type 0 (e.g. Fin n) and I : Type u (where u is the universe of the rings, modules etc.) (e.g, the set PrimeSpectrum R). If possible, allowing both of these cases is useful, because working with Fin n is nicer than working with ULift.{u} (Fin n). If it is not possible (we recently changed this for docs#AlgebraicGeometry.AffineSpace because performance was horrible), we choose I : Type u for sake of generality.

Note that it is important to develop e.g. the theory of abelian groups in any universe u. Otherwise, we could not work with definitions like docs#AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.EllAdicCohomology even if we start with X : Scheme.{0}.
(We will eventually be able to show that the groups here are u-small, but it will still take us a considerable amount of work. It is in progress though!)

I also find ModuleCat.extendScalars very difficult to use in practice. The issue is that docs#ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.obj is defined as ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (ModuleCat.of S S)) ⊗[R] M. So if we already have an instance [Algebra R S], then the instances about ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (ModuleCat.of S S)) are not definitionally equal to the instances about S. In this case, ModuleCat.ExtendScalars.obj becomes almost impossible to use.

For example, if S is a flat R-algebra, then we only know Module.Flat R ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (ModuleCat.of S S)) via a linearEquiv.

import Mathlib

universe u u'

variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (S : Type u') [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]

example [Module.Flat R S] :
    Module.Flat R ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (ModuleCat.of S S)) := by
  let e : (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap R S)).obj (ModuleCat.of S S) ≃ₗ[R] S :=
    { __ := AddEquiv.refl S
      map_smul' := by simp [Algebra.smul_def] }
  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv e
